resources.string: Deprecated signature algorithms (SHA1withRSA); insufficient key length; predictable ECDSA nonces; key reuse across purposes.
2048-bit RSA or P-256 ECDSA used. Meets NIST minimum for signatures through 2030+.
512-bit RSA key. Factorable with public cloud computing in hours. Any attacker can forge signatures.
Separate RSA key pairs for encryption and signing. Key separation per NIST SP 800-57 enforced.
RSA key pair used for both decryption and signing. Cross-protocol attacks can recover private key material.
Nonce derived deterministically per RFC 6979. Same nonce never reused. Private key cannot be extracted.
ECDSA nonce k hardcoded to 1 for two different messages. Private key fully recoverable with simple algebra from two signatures.
SHA256withECDSA used. NIST-approved, provides 128-bit security, faster than RSA.
Document signed with SHA1withRSA. SHA-1 is broken for signatures — collision attacks enable signature forgery.
4. Same Key for Signing and Decryption
